title: GradCheck: Analyzing classifier guidance gradients for conditional diffusion sampling
property: image class (four sport-ball classes), used to study gradient quality at noisy inputs
reads: MobileNetV3 small on the 3x64x64 noisy image x_t or on its one-step denoised estimate
trained_on: SportBalls synthetic images: one classifier on clean images, one on noisy images at uniformly sampled DDPM timesteps
gradient_enters: Mean shift mu' = mu + s Sigma ||mu|| g/||g||, with g = grad log p(y|x_t), s = 0.04, through all sampling steps of an unconditional pixel DDPM
unseen: no: all four classes are in classifier training and every run targets the class baseball
headline: Target accuracy (0 to 100%, higher better) and FID (lower better) on 64 images: noise-trained classifier 96.88% and 26.641; clean-trained 15.63% and 126.526; clean-trained read through x0-hat plus ADAM 85.94% and 24.348; pixel DDPM on SportBalls
copy_or_avoid: Train checkers on noisy inputs at the steps they push; do not treat a steady gradient as a meaningful one, since ADAM alone gave high cosine and no gain, and test early steps with a step-window ablation (inferred)

quotes.text: We train one robust and one non-robust MobileNet
The SportBalls data set (3x64x64) is synthetically created
as a potential solution for obtaining meaningful gradients earlier in the guided sampling process
The non-robust classifier is trained and evaluated on clean images and achieves a validation accuracy of 99.2%
based on uniform sampling of time steps and the noise schedule of the DDPM model
the non-robust classifier achieves a validation accuracy of 26.65% on the noisy DDPM latents
quotes.supports: trained_on: clean classifier at noisy inputs

quotes.text: The robust classifier achieves a validation accuracy on the noisy latents of 64.1%
We use this gradient normalization for our experiments, as it keeps the scaling factor s constant across all experimental setups
a step size of s = 0.04 and a batch size of 64
The target class for all experiments is the class “baseball”
we can infer that the non-robust classifier has almost random gradients for most of the denoising process
quotes.supports: conclusion on clean-trained classifier at noisy inputs

quotes.text: the robust classifier (red) having a high and fairly consistent cosine similarity over time
results in almost unchanged metrics compared to no modifications
The gradients have to be meaningful and stable over time
The classifier accuracy is based on the same classifier used in the guidance process

Figure 2, read from image: x0-hat cosine about 0.05 near t=1000, 0.4 to 0.5 from t=750 to 300, 0.85 at t=0; ADAM alone about 0.9
